title: Blue Hour and Aftermath
premise: Yara Blackwood, once the conservatory's most celebrated piano prodigy, returns two decades after his silent disappearance to work as its janitor, invisible among the students he might have been. When demolition of the east wing uncovers a box of letters his late mentor, Odile Ferrant, never sent him—letters revealing she fought the institution that destroyed him and loved him in ways duty forbade her to say—he must finally break his own silence. Confronting the director who inherited Odile's compromises, Yara plays the unfinished sonata from her final letter in the empty hall on the eve of demolition, saying goodbye out loud at last, and walks out carrying not the past but its permission.
about_author: Wren Okonkwo is a former conservatory custodian turned novelist whose work examines the quiet violence of institutions and the inheritances we refuse. They write in the blue hour, when the day's duties end and the unsaid becomes audible.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Working nights as a janitor in the conservatory that once crowned him a prodigy, he catalogs dust, broken chairs, and everything unsaid—his ruined hands, his vanished career, the mentor whose name no one speaks. When demolition notices appear, a student recognizes him, cracking his careful invisibility. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into compulsion; the past is no longer containable.

chapters.title: Behind the Wardrobe
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with interpolated letters from Odile Ferrant. Clearing the east wing, he finds a box wedged behind his old practice-room wardrobe: forty years of undelivered letters to him, charting her battle against the directorate that broke them both and the love she chose duty over. He learns his disappearance was engineered, not chosen. Emotional beat: grief igniting into fury; inheritance arrives as accusation.

chapters.title: What the Director Kept
chapters.summary: Yara confronts Director Anselm Voss, now old and decorated, who received copies of every letter and buried them to protect the institution—and himself. Their duel over memory, power, and who gets to narrate a life escalates until Voss offers Yara hush money and a place in the official history. Emotional beat: climax; Yara refuses both, choosing truth over the corrupted inheritance offered to him.

chapters.title: Blue Hour, Out Loud
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On demolition eve, he unlocks the hall, sits at Odile's surviving piano, and plays her unfinished sonata from the last letter—aloud, badly, completely—as staff and students gather in the blue-hour light. He reads her final words to the room, forgives her, forgives himself, and lets the building go. Emotional beat: resolution; goodbye spoken, love claimed against duty, the future inherited clean.
